amendments.known_risk: the reviewer reports marking far HFR duplicates as different in X7, while development mostly reads them as same (18 such pairs in X3-X6 marked same at 2 km or more). Development and test may disagree on that slice; the far-duplicate definition is to be settled afterwards by a blind recheck of the whole slice
amendments.what: the Oyo label file (development key x6) changed after this preregistration: three pairs (Ilogbo Health Post, God Mercy Clinic, Blessed Hospital), the far-duplicate lookalikes reported as X6's model errors, were changed from same_entity to different at 06:06-06:08 UTC. Development reads them as exported through restore_exported.json, giving back X6's 148 same / 100 different. The rule is unchanged

expectation: the ungated decider may again auto-match dense-city lookalikes in Lagos; the gate should stop those, at a cost in coverage and possibly in the error-per-settled-pair bound
known_risks: one reviewer, and a smaller pack (150) to keep review load down; with about 60-80 different pairs, one false merge can put the Wilson upper bound over 5%
informative needs at least 60 different pairs; X4's Lagos review band was 23% different, so most different pairs come from the lookalike and near-miss kinds
GATE_N was chosen on development labels that include X4's Lagos pairs; the X7 pairs are disjoint from them but from the same city
the output file's schema field reads arche.x6_gate.v1 because X7 runs X6's code unchanged
the X6 lookalike labels (a far HFR duplicate of a facility marked same) are kept as exported in development
question: On fresh Lagos pairs, does the gated decider pass X6's rule, and does the ungated one?

arms.control: the same combiner without the gate; reported, not tested
arms.gated: the X5 control combiner [cross-encoder logit, log1p km, LGA agree through the alias table, coordinates missing]; a pair whose GRID3 point has more than 15 other HFR facilities within 2 km (HFR national coordinates, the pair's HFR record excluded) is never auto-matched, though it may still be auto-rejected
arms.reference: match-everything, scored under the same rule; it must fail

rule.cross_encoder: X6's models unchanged (Edo, Kano, Ondo, Lagos, FCT and Oyo held out of training); weights pinned below
rule.development: 1,558 labelled pairs: X6's 1,310 development labels plus the Oyo pack as exported (2 unresolved dropped); no relabel
rule.error_bound: errors among auto-decided <= 3% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 10%
rule.false_merge_bound: different pairs auto-matched / all different pairs <= 2% and Wilson 95% upper bound <= 5%
rule.gate: GATE_N = 15, fixed from development out-of-fold predictions before the Oyo pack was built: on 1,310 labels it leaves 1-2 of 6 out-of-fold false merges with X5's models, and out-of-fold coverage about 0.71 against 0.74-0.76 ungated
rule.informative: void unless the test holds at least 60 different pairs
rule.pass: informative, and every seed of the gated arm meets fewer_held, error_bound and false_merge_bound on the whole pack
rule.population: the X7 pack (data/review_packs/nigeria_facilities_lagos_x7_2026-11-23, 150 Lagos pairs: 80 review_band, 35 lookalike, 35 near_miss) marked same_entity or different; read once, after this file
rule.review_band: reported on its own: every seed of the gated arm meets fewer_held and error_bound on the review_band pairs
secondary: development out-of-fold false merges, gated and ungated
rule.thresholds: 5-fold out-of-fold development predictions of the ungated combiner (x3_level.fit); the gate is applied after
rule.unchanged_from_x6: features, GATE_N = 15, thresholds, bounds and pass rule are X6's, unchanged after X6's result was read

test.blind: the reviewer sees neither the engine's decision nor the pair's kind
test.construction: data/scripts/build_x7_pack.py: every GRID3 and HFR record in the X4 Lagos pack, and each GRID3 record's own HFR twin, removed first; then build_x4_pack.py with BAND 80, STRESS 35: 80 of the 190 remaining engine review pairs (salted-hash order), 35 lookalike and 35 near_miss

why: X6's gate failed in Oyo on errors per settled pair (it held back correct matches; no false merge in either arm), and the ungated decider passed. Oyo did not need the gate. Lagos, where X4 failed with 7-9 false merges, is the case it was built for. The rule is kept unchanged rather than redefined after a failure
